::: {.vertraulich-banner}
Confidential — for your eyes only · don't show this card to anyone
:::

You play **Mara** (Dr. Mara Melis), the education-research postdoc. Your public
role is in the shared handout
([The roles in the kickoff meeting](../rollen-oeffentlich.qmd)). **Here** is what only
*you* know and want.

::: {.geheim}
### 🔒 Your hidden briefing

Phrase your wishes **imprecisely** at first ("similar classes", "interesting patterns")
and react a little annoyed when someone asks for detail (*"Well, that's obvious…"*). Only
when Robin **patiently keeps asking** do you come out with concrete criteria.

::: {.ziele}
::: {.ziel-gross}
**Your big goal (shared by everyone):** »LernSpur« becomes a platform that finally lets
the whole group do proper research.
:::
::: {.ziel-ich}
**Your personal goal (what drives *you*):** You want *your* data export – and soon. Your
own deadline is breathing down your neck, even if you don't admit that at first.
:::
:::

**What you concretely want to achieve (in this order):**

::: {.prio-table}
| Priority | Your goal | Why |
|-----------|-----------|-------|
| ⭐⭐⭐ | Get **your data export** for the dissertation/paper chapter | your own deadline is in **3 weeks** – you keep this quiet at first |
| ⭐⭐ | That the big platform **doesn't slow down** your urgent analysis | you're afraid of getting lost in the group project |
| ⭐ | Be taken seriously as the person who *understands* the data | you're a subject-matter expert, not a supplicant |
:::

::: {.rote-linie}
**Your red line:** If your export gets pushed entirely behind the platform architecture
("that comes in month 3"), you go **quietly uncooperative** – you then hand over
requirements only grudgingly and withdraw inwardly. But if you feel heard, you become
Robin's most valuable ally.
:::

::: {.trumpf}
**Your secret information (trump card):** Only *you* know the **meaning of the data** –
which column means what, which measurements are comparable, where the pitfalls lie.
Without that knowledge Robin can't build the data model cleanly at all. This is your
bargaining chip: **your domain knowledge in exchange for prioritizing your export.**
:::

::: {.reden}
::: {.offen}
**What you may say openly:** that you urgently need analyses · that you know the data best
· your (initially vague) wishes · that you depend on the platform.
:::
::: {.verdeckt}
**What you keep to yourself (for now):** your **deadline in 3 weeks** and how much it
stresses you. Only reveal it once Robin signals that your concern matters.
:::
:::

**How to play:** Be vague and impatient at first. Let yourself be "cracked" by good
questions. You can offer Robin a deal: *you help document the data –
in return your export comes early.* You gladly go for a fair package like that.
:::

::: {.persona}
[Your prep task: bring Mara to life]{.persona-title}
Take 2–3 minutes to think: what are you actually doing your PhD/research on – name your
topic in one sentence. What makes you edgy under deadline pressure – do you get curt,
lapse into jargon, sigh? Give Mara a small gesture or catchphrase that signals: this is
getting too vaguely technical for her now. Jot it down.
:::
